transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose it’s the worrying, mostly. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but once it gets started I have a hard time turning it off. Even if I’ve made my list, checked the dates, and done everything I reasonably can, my mind just keeps going over it. Does that make sense?
Is the worrying you experience limited to specific situations or events, or does it happen more generally throughout the day, even when there isn’t a clear reason?

It’s more general, I think. I mean, there are things that set it off, but it doesn’t stay neatly with one thing. My mind will go from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the gutters need looking at… and then suddenly those small things feel like they could turn into something much bigger. I know that may sound a bit silly, but that’s how it seems to move through the day.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, or muscle tension, especially when you're worrying?

Yes… I suppose I do, though it’s not dramatic or anything. I just feel sort of wound up sometimes, even at home in my own living room. I’ll be on the phone and notice I’m tapping my fingers, or I’ll get up and straighten something that doesn’t really need straightening, just because sitting still feels a bit jumpy. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
About how often do you experience these worries and physical symptoms? Do they occur on most days, or come and go more sporadically?

I’d say it’s been fairly regular… not every single minute, of course, and I don’t want to overstate it. But it’s been going on for about seven months now, since shortly after my friend died and I was trying to keep our projects moving. It sort of became part of the day more often than I’d like. Does that answer it properly?
Do you find that your anxiety or worry is focused on a variety of different events or activities, such as work, family, health, or everyday responsibilities, rather than just one specific thing?

Yes, I think that’s fair to say. It isn’t just one thing I worry about. My mind sort of roams from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the gutters need fixing… things like that. And then, even though I know they’re ordinary concerns, they start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger. I’m not sure if I’m explaining that quite right.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop the worrying, even when you recognize that the concerns might be exaggerated or unnecessary?

Yes… I’m afraid that is probably the main thing, really. I can tell myself, “You’ve made the list, you’ve checked the dates, you’ve done what you can,” and I do know that logically. But once the worrying starts, I don’t seem able to switch it off very well.

I mean, I’m not completely out of control or anything, but it keeps circling back, even when I know it’s not useful. That’s actually more or less why I thought I should come in. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense anxiety or fear that comes on very quickly and feels overwhelming, even if there isn’t an obvious trigger?

I don’t think so… not in that very sudden, overwhelming way you’re describing. I do get anxious, but it feels more like it builds or lingers rather than coming out of nowhere all at once.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean—would that be like a panic sort of episode? I wouldn’t say I’ve really had that.
Have you ever felt the need to do things a certain way, or repeat certain actions, because it eased your mind or stopped a worry, even if it was just temporary?

Not really, no… I mean, I like things to be orderly, and I might check my diary or a list if I’m feeling unsettled, but I don’t think I have to repeat things in a particular way to make the worry go away.

At least, nothing that feels like a ritual or anything like that. Does that make sense?
Would you say that your anxiety or feeling of being on edge is present even when there’s no specific reason or trigger, just a general sense of worry throughout the day?

Yes, I think so… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s not always tied to one clear thing happening right then.

My mind just sort of wanders from one concern to another — the exhibition schedule, then my daughter’s travel plans, then something like whether the gutters at the house need fixing. And then small things start to feel as if they could turn into something much bigger if I don’t keep thinking about them.

So yes, I suppose there is often a general sense of being on edge during the day. Does that answer what you mean?

Have you ever felt driven to perform certain actions or rituals repeatedly because you thought something bad might happen if you didn’t, or to reduce your anxiety, even if you knew it might not make much sense?

No, I don’t think so. I can’t really think of anything I do like a ritual because I believe something bad will happen if I don’t.

I might double-check something ordinary now and then, but not repeatedly, and not in that “I have to do this or else” sort of way. At least, I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or welcome, but they keep coming back, even though you try not to think about them?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, where a thought feels unwanted and keeps forcing itself back in.

I mean, I do worry about things, of course, and sometimes the same concern comes round again, but it feels more like ordinary worrying than a thought I’m trying to push away and can’t. I’m not sure if that distinction makes sense, but I wouldn’t say I have intrusive thoughts like that.
Has this worrying or feeling on edge made it harder for you to do things you need to do, like work, take care of responsibilities, or enjoy time with family and friends?

A little, yes… though I’m still managing, I don’t want to overstate it.

I still keep up with the garden and I go to book club, things like that. But I have noticed I’m sometimes less prepared than I used to be, and with the exhibition planning I’ve started turning down some parts of it because it just feels harder to manage than before.

It’s not that I’ve stopped doing things, exactly. It’s more that I’m doing a bit less, or I need more effort to keep up. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Has your worrying ever caused significant distress or made it much harder for you to function in any important part of your life, like at work, socially, or in your relationships?

I wouldn’t say it’s made things impossible, or anything like that. I’m still keeping up with my garden, and I do go to book club, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But… yes, I suppose it has made some things harder. I’ve noticed I’m not always as prepared as I used to be, and with the exhibition planning I’ve started saying no to parts of it because it just feels harder to manage than before.

So, maybe not “significant” in a dramatic way, but it is affecting me a bit. Does that answer what you mean?
Would you say your worrying is mainly about real-life concerns, like everyday responsibilities or events, rather than thoughts or images that feel intrusive and unwanted?

Yes, I think that’s right. It’s more about real-life things, not images or thoughts that feel strange or unwanted.

My mind just sort of roams, I suppose… from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the gutters on the house need fixing. And then little things can start to feel as though they might turn into something much bigger if I don’t keep on top of them.

But it’s ordinary things, really. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of worry you mean?
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you're feeling anxious or worried?

I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that, no. I mean, I hope I’m not more irritable with people… I don’t think so.

Maybe I get a bit short in my own head when I’m wound up, but I don’t think I’m snapping at anyone particularly. At least, no one’s said anything to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often have trouble sleeping because your mind is racing or you're unable to relax, even when you're tired?

I’m not sure, really. I mean, I do have the odd night where it takes me a while to settle, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s often because my mind is racing.

Sometimes I’m just… awake, and then I start thinking because I’m awake, if that makes sense. But I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I don’t think sleep is the main problem for me. Is that helpful?
